vocabulary.meaning_en: a statement that something is wrong or not good enough
vocabulary.note_ar: من الفعل complain = يشتكي؛ نقول make a complaint وليس do
vocabulary.example: I made a complaint about the noise.
vocabulary.note_en: From the verb "complain"; we say "make a complaint", not "do".

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say that you are not happy about something
vocabulary.example: He complained about the cold food.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the team that helps customers
vocabulary.example: Customer service answered my email quickly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a promise that something is good or will happen
vocabulary.example: I guarantee you'll love this pizza.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a written legal promise to repair or replace a product
vocabulary.example: My laptop is still under warranty.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper that proves you paid
vocabulary.example: Keep the receipt in case it breaks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money paid back to you
vocabulary.example: I asked for a full refund.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take or send something back
vocabulary.example: You can return it within 30 days.

vocabulary.meaning_en: giving something back and getting another
vocabulary.example: They offered me an exchange instead of a refund.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to fix something that is broken
vocabulary.example: Can you repair my phone screen?

vocabulary.meaning_en: not working; in pieces
vocabulary.example: The lift is broken again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: harmed, so it is not in good condition
vocabulary.note_ar: قد يبقى الشيء التالف يعمل رغم الضرر، أما broken فيعني أنه لا يعمل أو انكسر
vocabulary.example: The box arrived damaged.
vocabulary.note_en: A damaged thing may still work; "broken" means it doesn't work or is in pieces.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not working because of a problem from the factory
vocabulary.note_ar: fault = خطأ / عيب؛ ليس خطأ المستخدم
vocabulary.example: The charger was faulty, so I sent it back.
vocabulary.note_en: fault = a problem or defect; it is not the user's fault.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put a new thing in place of an old one
vocabulary.example: We can't repair it, but we'll replace it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a set of rules a company follows
vocabulary.example: What is your return policy?
vocabulary.note_en: Different from "politics" (the affairs of governments and countries).

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person in charge of a shop or team
vocabulary.example: I'd like to speak to the manager.
vocabulary.note_en: From "manage" (to be in charge of something).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who helps someone or works in a shop
vocabulary.note_ar: من assist = يساعد؛ shop assistant = بائع في محل
vocabulary.example: The shop assistant helped me find my size.
vocabulary.note_en: From "assist" (to help); shop assistant = a person who serves customers in a shop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the place in a shop where staff help customers
vocabulary.example: Ask at the service desk on the ground floor.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a phone number for quick help
vocabulary.example: Call our 24-hour hotline.

vocabulary.meaning_en: your opinion that helps someone improve
vocabulary.example: Thanks for your feedback on our app.
vocabulary.note_en: feed (give) + back (return): information given back about something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the feeling of being happy with something
vocabulary.note_ar: من satisfy = يُرضي؛ customer satisfaction = رضا العملاء
vocabulary.example: Customer satisfaction is our priority.
vocabulary.note_en: From "satisfy" (to make someone happy with something); customer satisfaction = how happy customers are.

vocabulary.meaning_en: words saying you are sorry
vocabulary.example: We received a letter of apology.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a time when something is late; to make late
vocabulary.example: Sorry for the delay.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something done wrongly
vocabulary.example: There's a mistake on my bill.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that causes difficulty
vocabulary.example: Ali explained his problem to the agent.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a way to fix a problem
vocabulary.example: We need a quick solution.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an answer or reaction
vocabulary.example: They promised a quick response.
vocabulary.note_en: The verb is "respond" (to answer or react).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper or page with spaces to write information
vocabulary.example: Please fill in this form.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an office where people answer customer calls
vocabulary.example: She works in a call centre.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who answers customers for a company
vocabulary.example: The agent gave me a reference number.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to manage to speak to someone or arrive somewhere
vocabulary.example: I couldn't reach anyone on the phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to write information in a form
vocabulary.note_ar: fill in بريطاني، fill out أمريكي
vocabulary.example: Fill out the form and sign it.
vocabulary.note_en: "Fill in" is British; "fill out" is American.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very annoyed because you can't change a situation
vocabulary.example: I was frustrated after two hours on hold.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling strong displeasure
vocabulary.example: Angry, Ali went back to the market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: worried and a little afraid
vocabulary.example: A nervous assistant answered the phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an exciting or unusual experience
vocabulary.example: Our trip was a real adventure.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to not go near something
vocabulary.example: Next time, I'll stay away from glowing stalls.

fine_lines.title: guarantee vs warranty
fine_lines.explanation_ar: guarantee وعد بأن المنتج جيد أو أن شيئاً سيحدث، قد تسمعه في إعلان أو من البائع، وليس عقداً قانونياً، ويمكن استخدامه في أي شيء. warranty وثيقة أو عقد قانوني مكتوب ومحدد بمدة، تلتزم فيه الشركة بإصلاح المنتج أو استبداله أو رد المال. لذلك عندما قال البائع under guarantee فهم علي أنه مجرد وعد بدون شهادة ضمان.

examples.sentence: I guarantee you'll like this pizza.
The TV has a two-year warranty, so they repaired it for free.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A guarantee is a promise that a product is good or that something will happen; you may hear it in an ad or from a seller. It is not a legal contract and can be used for anything. A warranty is a written legal document for a fixed time, where the company must repair or replace the product or give your money back. So when the seller said "under guarantee", Ali understood it was only a promise, with no warranty certificate.

fine_lines.title: broken vs damaged vs faulty
fine_lines.explanation_ar: broken مكسور أو لا يعمل. damaged فيه ضرر أو تلف (خدش، كسر، بلل) وقد يبقى يعمل أو لا يعمل. faulty به عيب من المصنع، أي ليس المستخدم من أفسده، لذلك يحق لك غالباً الإرجاع أو الاستبدال.

examples.sentence: I dropped my glasses and now they're broken.
The car was badly damaged in the accident.
The new watch was faulty and stopped working the next day.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Broken" = in pieces or not working. "Damaged" = harmed in some way (scratched, cracked, wet); it may or may not still work. "Faulty" = has a defect from the factory, so it's not the user's fault, and you can usually return or exchange it.

fine_lines.title: policy vs politics
fine_lines.explanation_ar: policy مجموعة قواعد تتبعها شركة أو متجر (سياسة الإرجاع مثلاً). politics سياسة الدول والحكومات والأحزاب.

examples.sentence: The shop's policy allows exchanges within 14 days.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A policy is a set of rules that a company or shop follows (for example, a return policy). Politics is about governments, countries and political parties.

fine_lines.title: make vs do (collocations)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: بعض الكلمات تأتي مع فعل معين دائماً كمتلازمة لفظية (collocation)، مثل «خطأ فادح» في العربية. نقول make a complaint و make the bed و make a mistake، ولا نقول do a complaint. احفظها كما هي.

examples.sentence: Make your bed before you leave.
I do my homework every evening.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Some words always go with a certain verb as a fixed pair (a collocation). We say "make a complaint", "make the bed" and "make a mistake", not "do a complaint". Learn these pairs as they are.

fine_lines.title: fill in vs fill out
fine_lines.explanation_ar: نفس المعنى (يملأ بيانات استمارة). fill in أشيع في بريطانيا، و fill out أشيع في أمريكا.

examples.sentence: Please fill in your name and address.
The agent gave him a form to fill out.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning (write your details on a form). "Fill in" is more common in Britain; "fill out" is more common in the US.

expressions.meaning_ar: يماطل شخصاً / يراوغه ولا يعطيه جواباً واضحاً
expressions.example: The company gave me the runaround when I asked for a refund.
expressions.meaning_en: keep delaying someone and avoid giving a clear answer

expressions.example: I want to make a complaint about the service.
expressions.meaning_en: formally say you are unhappy with something

expressions.example: Is the phone still under warranty?
expressions.meaning_en: still covered by a promise or warranty to repair it

expressions.example: The hotel sent us a letter of apology.
I want a refund, or at least an exchange.
expressions.meaning_en: or if not that, then something smaller

expressions.example: After many mistakes, the story had a happy ending.
We got home safely, and the adventure was over.

grammar.title: Reported questions with question words
grammar.explanation_ar: في السؤال الحقيقي يأتي الفعل المساعد بعد أداة الاستفهام (Where is the key?). لكن في الكلام المنقول لا نسأل، بل نحكي ما حدث، فتصبح أداة الاستفهام رابطاً فقط ويأتي بعدها الفاعل ثم الفعل، بدون علامة استفهام، مع الحفاظ على زمن الماضي. ونغيّر الضمائر منطقياً كما في العربية.
examples: Ali asked, "Where is the key?" → Ali asked where the key was.
"How does it work?" → She asked how it worked.
Mona asked, "Where is my school bag?" → Mona asked where her school bag was.
grammar.explanation_en: In a real question, the auxiliary verb comes after the question word (Where is the key?). In reported speech we are not asking, we are telling what happened, so the question word just links the sentences and is followed by subject + verb, with no question mark, and the tense moves into the past. Change the pronouns in a logical way.

grammar.title: Starting a sentence with an adjective (literary style)
grammar.explanation_ar: الكاتب المحترف يبدأ أحياناً بالصفة ثم فاصلة ثم الجملة، ليرسم الحالة النفسية للبطل قبل الفعل (مثل الحال في العربية: «غاضباً، عاد علي إلى السوق»). الفاصلة بعد الصفة ضرورية.
examples: Angry, Ali went back to the market.
Frustrated, he spoke to the manager.
Sad and alone, the boy sat in the dark.
grammar.explanation_en: Good writers sometimes begin with an adjective, then a comma, then the sentence, to show how the character feels before the action. The comma after the adjective is necessary.

grammar.title: Reported speech: keep the past tense
grammar.explanation_ar: عند نقل كلام في الماضي نحافظ على الزمن: can تصبح could و will تصبح would. ونضع فاصلة قبل but عند ربط جملتين.
examples: "We can't repair it, but we will replace it." → The manager told Ali (that) they couldn't repair it, but they would replace it.
grammar.explanation_en: When reporting past speech, keep the past tense: can becomes could, and will becomes would. Use a comma before "but" when joining two sentences.

questions.question: A written legal promise to repair a product for a fixed time is a:
questions.explanation_ar: warranty عقد قانوني مكتوب ومحدد بمدة، أما guarantee فهي وعد.
questions.explanation_en: A warranty is a written legal contract for a fixed time; a guarantee is just a promise.

questions.question: Ali wanted to ___ a complaint.
questions.explanation_en: The correct collocation is "make a complaint".

questions.question: The watch stopped working because of a problem from the factory. It was:
questions.explanation_en: Faulty = has a defect from the factory.

questions.question: Ali asked, "Where is the key?" → Ali asked ___.
questions.explanation_ar: في السؤال المنقول يأتي الفاعل ثم الفعل بعد أداة الاستفهام، مع الحفاظ على الماضي.
questions.explanation_en: In a reported question, the subject comes before the verb after the question word, and we keep the past tense.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the literary style correctly?
choices: Angry Ali went back to the market.
Angry, Ali went back to the market.
Ali angry, went back to the market.
questions.explanation_ar: نبدأ بالصفة ثم فاصلة ثم الجملة الأساسية.
questions.explanation_en: Start with the adjective, then a comma, then the main sentence.

questions.question: "What is your return ___?" (the shop's rules)
questions.explanation_ar: policy = سياسة المتجر، أما politics فسياسة الدول.
questions.explanation_en: Policy = a shop's rules; politics = government affairs.

questions.question: The company kept delaying and never gave me a clear answer. They gave me the ___.
questions.explanation_ar: give someone the runaround = يماطل ويراوغ.
questions.explanation_en: give someone the runaround = keep delaying and avoid a clear answer.

questions.question: In American English, you usually ___ a form.
questions.explanation_ar: fill out أمريكي، fill in بريطاني.
questions.explanation_en: "Fill out" is American; "fill in" is British.

questions.question: The manager said, "We can't repair it." → The manager said they ___ repair it.
questions.explanation_ar: نحافظ على زمن الماضي: can't تصبح couldn't.
questions.explanation_en: Keep the past tense: can't becomes couldn't.

questions.question: "Satisfaction" comes from the verb:
questions.explanation_en: Satisfy = make someone happy with something; satisfaction is the noun.
